ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is the diameter of the circumcircle $\odot O$ of $\triangle ABC$. If $\angle ACB = 50^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BD,\\
since AD is the diameter of the circumcircle $\odot O$ of $\triangle ABC$,\\
therefore $\angle ABD=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle D=\angle C=50^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BAD=90^\circ-\angle D=90^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: A is at the top of the circle, D at the bottom on the same vertical line through O, and B and C lie on the circle with chords AB, AC, and BC shown. Add the auxiliary chord BD. From the text, AD is a diameter, so by Thales’ theorem ∠ABD = 90°. Since A, B, C, D are concyclic, ∠ACB and ∠ADB subtend the same chord AB, so ∠ADB = 50°. In triangle ABD, compute ∠BAD = 180° - 90° - 50° = 40°.
